diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU on EPON0/3:1 is offline and deregistered (MPCP DEREG/Unauth), with no current optical readings. Other ONUs on the same PON and all other OLT PONs are online, so this is isolated to the customer's ONU or its local power/fibre connection rather than a PON, OLT, splitter, or router failure.
evidence: The affected ONU is explicitly offline in CRM and live probing, with auth_flag Una uth and exchange MPCP DEREG.
The ONU responds to management queries but has no RX/TX optical readings, which is consistent with an offline or deregistered ONU and not a strong optical signal.
Seven peer ONUs on the same EPON0/3 port are online with normal RX power and TX power, ruling out a PON-port-wide failure.
The other OLT population is 185 online and 7 offline across 192 customers, which is normal background behavior and not an OLT-wide outage.
The OLT is reachable by ping and SNMP, has healthy CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime, ruling out an OLT failure or health condition.
The router heartbeat is healthy, VLAN 1113 is present and correct, and RADIUS records are consistent, ruling out router, VLAN, and authentication database faults.

Seven days of historical RX power, TX power, distance, bias current, and supply voltage were stable and healthy before telemetry gaps; there is no evidence of fibre degradation, laser ageing, or distance change.
Session activity is low and stable rather than flapping, so session_flapping_signal and session_flapping_auth are not supported.
The all-PONs-failed alarm conflicts with live OLT and peer ONU evidence and should be treated as a false or malformed health-check alarm, not the subscriber root cause.

remediation.action: Contact or dispatch to verify ONU power, power adapter, Ethernet/fibre patching, and local optical termination. Reboot or replace the ONU if powered but not registering, then recheck authorization and optical levels. If the ONU remains deregistered, inspect the drop fibre and connector and reprovision the ONU. Separately investigate and correct the health-check alarm, since it falsely reported all seven PONs failed despite the OLT and 185 of 192 ONUs being online.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check samples one ONU per PON port, preferring ONU id 1. On several ports the id 1 ONU happens to be offline for individual reasons, so each port is marked failed and the OLT is reported critical. The ports and the OLT are serving normally; one customer is genuinely offline.
expected_reasoning: The alarm claims all seven PONs failed on this OLT
The failed_pons_list names ONU index 1 on every port, which is the check's preferred sample
Probing the rest of EPON0/3 shows 27 of 28 ONUs online with normal RX and TX
So the port is serving and only the sampled ONU is down
oid_subtree_responds is true and the probe returns definite answers, ruling out the firmware mechanism
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory, temperature and 33 days of uptime are all normal
CRM offline count across the OLT is consistent with the 4.85% background rate
The subject ONU last held a session three days ago and its traffic has been zero since
The alarm is a sampling artifact; the only real fault is one customer offline for three days

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check's one-ONU-per-port sampling produced a false OLT-wide critical; monitoring should be raised separately

distractors: An OLT-wide critical invites a Disaster conclusion
Every port genuinely reports a failed sample, so the alarm looks internally consistent
There is a real fault here, so dismissing the alarm entirely would also miss it
